title: Signature: Soundscape Primer
description: This Signature primer designs a soundscape from three separate layer tracks, following the public edition's rule that biophony, geophony, and anthrophony are stored separately and mixed only arithmetically. A Signature soundscape is specified by listing, for each layer, a level in decibels, a set of frequency bands, and a schedule of activity across the day, and the primer's model combines those inputs into a total level, a band-occupancy table, and an NDSI-style balance figure. The primer is a teaching design: a student enters layer values, watches the balance move, and learns why a soundscape dominated by one layer sounds the way it does. Every input is invented, every output is labelled a Signature model, and no sound file is shipped or claimed to be a recording of a real place.
body:
This Signature primer designs a soundscape from three separate layer tracks, following the public edition's rule that biophony, geophony, and anthrophony are stored separately and mixed only arithmetically. A Signature soundscape is specified by listing, for each layer, a level in decibels, a set of frequency bands, and a schedule of activity across the day, and the primer's model combines those inputs into a total level, a band-occupancy table, and an NDSI-style balance figure. The primer is a teaching design: a student enters layer values, watches the balance move, and learns why a soundscape dominated by one layer sounds the way it does. Every input is invented, every output is labelled a Signature model, and no sound file is shipped or claimed to be a recording of a real place.

Science proof

Science proof: the primer implements the published three-layer model and the published decibel-addition and NDSI arithmetic, applied to invented inputs. That combination, published formulas plus labelled invented inputs, is the standard form of a design model in soundscape teaching, and it is honest precisely because the formulas are public and the inputs are declared as designs.

Math proof

Math proof: for layers at 55, 50, and 60 dB, the combined level is 10 x log10(10^5.5 + 10^5 + 10^6) = 61.51 dB. The demo prints the three layer levels, the combined level 61.51 dB, and the anthrophony power share, 10^6 / (10^5.5 + 10^5 + 10^6) = 70.6 percent.

title: Signature: Forest Soundscape Model
description: This Signature model designs a forest soundscape as a schedule of virtual voices by height and hour. Canopy singers occupy higher bands at dawn, understorey singers occupy middle bands through the morning, ground frogs call at night, and wind through virtual leaves adds a broad geophony whose level follows a stated gust schedule. The model reports band occupancy, the busiest hour, and the overlap between layers, and it lets a student change the wind schedule and watch masking rise. The model is a design study, not a recording: its singers are invented, its parameters are stated, and any sound rendered from it is labelled SIMULATED. Its purpose is teaching forest soundscape structure and giving composers a layered forest template.
body:
This Signature model designs a forest soundscape as a schedule of virtual voices by height and hour. Canopy singers occupy higher bands at dawn, understorey singers occupy middle bands through the morning, ground frogs call at night, and wind through virtual leaves adds a broad geophony whose level follows a stated gust schedule. The model reports band occupancy, the busiest hour, and the overlap between layers, and it lets a student change the wind schedule and watch masking rise. The model is a design study, not a recording: its singers are invented, its parameters are stated, and any sound rendered from it is labelled SIMULATED. Its purpose is teaching forest soundscape structure and giving composers a layered forest template.

Science proof

Science proof: the model encodes the documented structure of real forest soundscapes: dawn peaks, height-layered singing, wind geophony, and seasonal thinning. By stating its schedules and bands explicitly, the model can be compared, layer by layer, with a real forest recording's spectrogram, which is the honest test of a soundscape design.

Math proof

Math proof: if virtual canopy birds occupy 5 bands, understorey birds occupy 4 bands, and 2 bands are shared, total occupied bands are 5 + 4 - 2 = 7 of 10, an occupancy of 70.0 percent. The demo prints canopy 5, understorey 4, shared 2, total occupied 7, and occupancy 70.0 percent.

title: Signature: Ocean Soundscape Model
description: This Signature model designs an ocean soundscape as a depth-layered system. Surface wave geophony is specified by a wave-period parameter, reef-like virtual shrimp add broadband crackle in shallow bands, virtual whale-like singers add long low-frequency phrases, and a deep sound channel parameter carries low-frequency energy over a stated distance. The model computes travel times in water, compares them with travel times in air, and reports which voices dominate each depth band. No ocean is recorded and no real whale is imitated as a field claim: the model is arithmetic and scheduling, and any rendered ocean sound is labelled SIMULATED. Its purpose is teaching why the ocean is a long-distance acoustic world and giving sound designers a deep-water template.
body:
This Signature model designs an ocean soundscape as a depth-layered system. Surface wave geophony is specified by a wave-period parameter, reef-like virtual shrimp add broadband crackle in shallow bands, virtual whale-like singers add long low-frequency phrases, and a deep sound channel parameter carries low-frequency energy over a stated distance. The model computes travel times in water, compares them with travel times in air, and reports which voices dominate each depth band. No ocean is recorded and no real whale is imitated as a field claim: the model is arithmetic and scheduling, and any rendered ocean sound is labelled SIMULATED. Its purpose is teaching why the ocean is a long-distance acoustic world and giving sound designers a deep-water template.

Science proof

Science proof: the model encodes the published physics of ocean sound: faster sound in water than in air, long low-frequency range, and the deep sound channel's trapping effect. Those are measured features of ocean acoustics, and the model states its speed and distance parameters so its travel-time figures can be checked by hand.

Math proof

Math proof: sound in seawater travels at roughly 1500 metres per second, about 1500 / 343 = 4.37 times the speed in air. A sound crossing 75 kilometres takes 75000 / 1500 = 50.0 seconds in water and 75000 / 343 = 218.7 seconds in air. The demo prints the ratio 4.37, water time 50.0 seconds, and air time 218.7 seconds.

title: Signature: Desert Wind Model
description: This Signature model designs a desert soundscape around wind. A virtual desert is specified by a wind schedule across the day, a dune-tone parameter for singing-dune-like low tones, and a sparse set of virtual animal voices scheduled at dawn, dusk, and night. The model computes the share of each hour occupied by biophony versus wind-only sound, and it shows how night-time stillness lets sparse voices carry further. The model is a design study: its desert is invented, its wind schedule is chosen, and any rendered desert sound is labelled SIMULATED. Its purpose is teaching the acoustics of quiet, open places and giving composers a desert template built from wind first and voices second.

title: Signature: Wetland Model
description: This Signature model designs a wetland soundscape as a chorus system. Virtual frogs are placed around a virtual pond, each with a call duration, period, and dominant frequency, and virtual marsh birds add booming and calling voices from reed beds. Water geophony is specified as rain patter and wind ripple levels, and the model computes total call rate, duty cycles, and the masking margin between the frog band and the water-noise band. The model is a teaching and composition design: it shows how a dense wetland chorus is organised, and it never claims to be a recording of a real wetland. Any rendered wetland sound is labelled SIMULATED.

This Signature model designs a wetland soundscape as a chorus system. Virtual frogs are placed around a virtual pond, each with a call duration, period, and dominant frequency, and virtual marsh birds add booming and calling voices from reed beds. Water geophony is specified as rain patter and wind ripple levels, and the model computes total call rate, duty cycles, and the masking margin between the frog band and the water-noise band. The model is a teaching and composition design: it shows how a dense wetland chorus is organised, and it never claims to be a recording of a real wetland. Any rendered wetland sound is labelled SIMULATED.

Science proof

Science proof: the model encodes the documented wetland pattern: dense frog choruses, reed-bed bird voices, and water geophony, with call rates and duty cycles as the organising numbers. Those numbers are the same quantities field researchers measure in real wetland choruses, so the model's outputs can be compared directly with published chorus figures.

title: Signature: Quiet City Model
description: This Signature model designs a city soundscape in which anthrophony is deliberately reduced. A virtual city block is specified with a baseline traffic level, a park refuge level, and a bird-voice layer, and the model computes the level difference between street and park, the intensity ratio that difference represents, and the NDSI-style balance in each zone. The model lets a planner test design moves, such as lowering traffic by a stated number of decibels or enlarging the park, and watch the balance move toward biophony. The city is invented, the numbers are design inputs, and every output is labelled a Signature model. Its purpose is teaching urban soundscape design and giving planners a simple, honest arithmetic for quiet-city arguments.

This Signature model designs a city soundscape in which anthrophony is deliberately reduced. A virtual city block is specified with a baseline traffic level, a park refuge level, and a bird-voice layer, and the model computes the level difference between street and park, the intensity ratio that difference represents, and the NDSI-style balance in each zone. The model lets a planner test design moves, such as lowering traffic by a stated number of decibels or enlarging the park, and watch the balance move toward biophony. The city is invented, the numbers are design inputs, and every output is labelled a Signature model. Its purpose is teaching urban soundscape design and giving planners a simple, honest arithmetic for quiet-city arguments.

Science proof

Science proof: the model's arithmetic is published decibel and NDSI arithmetic, and its qualitative direction, lower traffic and larger refuges mean more audible biophony, matches published urban soundscape findings. The model claims no quantitative prediction for any real city, and its documentation states that limit plainly.

Math proof: if a virtual street measures 65 dB and a virtual park measures 45 dB, the difference is 20 dB, an intensity ratio of 10^(20/10) = 100.0 times. The demo prints the difference 20 dB, the ratio 100.0, and the combined level of street and park heard together, 65.04 dB.

title: Signature: Rainforest Dawn Model
description: This Signature model designs a rainforest dawn as the densest virtual chorus in the suite. Sixty virtual species are assigned bands, time slots, and call rates, rain is scheduled as a geophony interruption, and the model reports total occupied bandwidth, the overlap that forces time-sharing, and the chorus's recovery time after the rain stops. The design rule is the acoustic niche rule: bands first, time slots second, and the model scores how well a given assignment follows it. The rainforest is invented, the species are virtual, and any rendered dawn sound is labelled SIMULATED. Its purpose is teaching dense-soundscape organisation at its most demanding and giving composers a rainforest template.

Sixty virtual species are assigned bands, time slots, and call rates, rain is scheduled as a geophony interruption, and the model reports total occupied bandwidth, the overlap that forces time-sharing, and the chorus's recovery time after the rain stops. The design rule is the acoustic niche rule: bands first, time slots second, and the model scores how well a given assignment follows it. The rainforest is invented, the species are virtual, and any rendered dawn sound is labelled SIMULATED. title: Signature: Ice Soundscape Model
description: This Signature model designs an Arctic-like soundscape from ice and seasonal life. Virtual sea ice is specified with cracking-event rates and low-frequency energy, wind over virtual tundra adds a steady hiss, and virtual seals and whales add seasonal calls under the ice and in open water. The model computes the open-water share as virtual ice cover falls, the wave-noise rise that follows, and the seasonal swing in biophony activity between summer and winter. The Arctic is invented as a model world, no real ice is recorded, and any rendered ice sound is labelled SIMULATED. Its purpose is teaching ice acoustics and seasonal soundscape change in extreme environments.

Science proof: the model encodes the documented Arctic pattern: ice-crack geophony, seasonal marine-mammal vocal activity, and soundscape change as ice cover retreats. Those patterns are published Arctic monitoring findings, reproduced here as a parameter-explicit design.

title: Signature: Savanna Model

A fire-recovery parameter thins the virtual community after a virtual burn and restores it over stated seasons, letting a student watch the soundscape recover in numbers. The savanna is invented, the herds are virtual, and any rendered savanna sound is labelled SIMULATED.

This Signature model designs a restored quiet park as a before-and-after comparison. A virtual degraded site is specified with low biophony power and high anthrophony power, a restoration step raises biophony power and lowers anthrophony power by stated amounts, and the model reports NDSI before and after, plus the improvement. A quiet-core parameter marks a virtual square of protected quiet inside the park, modelled on the public edition's One Square Inch idea, and the model reports the core's balance separately from the park's edge. The park is invented, the restoration step is a design input, and every output is labelled a Signature model, never a claim about a real park.

Science proof

Science proof: the model encodes the documented restoration pattern: acoustic richness recovering alongside vegetation and animal communities, and natural quiet protected as a conservation value. Its NDSI arithmetic is the published definition, applied to invented inputs, so its improvement figures describe the model, not a real site.

Math proof

Math proof: if virtual biophony power rises from 0.3 to 0.7 while anthrophony power falls from 0.5 to 0.2, NDSI rises from (0.3 - 0.5) / (0.3 + 0.5) = -0.25 to (0.7 - 0.2) / (0.7 + 0.2) = 0.56. The demo prints NDSI -0.25 before restoration and 0.56 after, plus the improvement, 0.56 - (-0.25) = 0.81.
